rabbi-chanina.name: Rabbi Ḥanina
rabbi-chanina.bio: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Ḥama, a student of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and a leading Amora of the first generation in the Land of Israel.
rabbi-chanina.prompt: A venerable sage in his 70s with a long white beard and a calm, upright bearing, a student of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi who lived to a great age, background Galilean limestone arches of Sepphoris and olive trees.

rabbi-oshaya.name: Rabbi Oshaya
rabbi-oshaya.bio: Early Amora of the Land of Israel, usually identified with Rabbi Hoshaya Rabba of Caesarea.
rabbi-oshaya.prompt: A scholarly sage in his 60s with a full grey beard and an earnest, searching look, scrolls of baraitot at his side, background limestone colonnades of Caesarea by the sea.

rav-ashi.name: Rav Ashi
rav-ashi.bio: Head of the academy at Mata Meḥasya, traditionally credited with editing the Babylonian Talmud.
rav-ashi.prompt: A dignified, wealthy and learned sage in his 60s with a well-kept grey beard and a composed, authoritative expression, holding an open scroll as the editor of the Talmud, background a large Babylonian academy hall with oil lamps.

rav-acha-brei-deravina.name: Rav Aḥa son of Ravina
rav-acha-brei-deravina.bio: Babylonian Amora of Rav Ashi’s generation; Rashi notes that he was a priest.
rav-acha-brei-deravina.prompt: A Babylonian scholar and priest in his 40s with a dark beard and a quick, good-humoured expression, a small purse of coins in his hand, background palm groves along the Euphrates.

rav-asi.name: Rav Asi
rav-asi.bio: Babylonian Amora of the first generation, a colleague of Rav and Shmuel.
rav-asi.prompt: A dignified Babylonian sage in his 60s with a full greying beard and a calm, deliberate expression, a dark wool mantle over a linen robe, as one of the early masters who sat alongside Rav and Shmuel. Mudbrick study house of a Babylonian town with oil lamps softly behind him.
